title: Final review of Phase 2 epic diff
description: Review the integrated Phase 2 diff: per-tick container isolation and the three spawn defences, one lease across local and cloud orchestrators, reconcile correctness against a live worker, and that run_event remained observability rather than becoming control. Verify against a REAL deployment and a REAL multi-container wave — Phase 1 shipped four defects that only live execution found.
notes:
2026-08-22 07:04 - Final review of the Phase 2 diff: 83 commits, 203 files, +36,529/-1,574 against origin/main. Review the DIFF, not the reports — the reports are the claims, the diff is the evidence.

Axes this epic earns, roughly in order of what it has actually got wrong before:
- CORRECTNESS AT THE SEAMS. Two waves collided in cloud/factory/src/run-workflow.ts (k24's cancellation seam and bne's run_event publishes) and the orchestrator hand-resolved both the source and the interleaved test file. Check that resolution specifically: the collected-events publish was deliberately placed BEFORE k24's cancellation return so a cancelled batch still reports what its containers produced. Verify both features are actually live and that the reconstructed test file tests both rather than merely compiling.
- ENFORCEMENT THAT CANNOT ACT. This epic's signature defect, hit four times: a budget that could not trip (cts), a revocation the next boot undid (gyl), a wave width printed but never enforced (kji), a stop that waited for a batch (k24). Look for the fifth instance rather than assuming there isn't one.
- SIGNALS THAT ARE TRUE AND MISREAD. Hit three times: a short id answered with a confident negative (c5i), a killed worker reporting done, a successful wave reporting stopped (074). Same question — is there a fourth?
- CLAIMS VS MEASUREMENTS. kuf and y45 both committed re-runnable harnesses and dated raw output. Check that what the docs and code comments assert matches what the committed artifacts actually show, especially any number quoted in a comment.
- PUBLIC REPO. Nothing operator-specific: no account ids, deployment URLs, vault or workspace ids, real bucket or database names, personal or work email addresses. The guard script passes, but it is an allowlist and this diff added benchmark artifacts.

Report severity and confidence per finding. You review; the orchestrator adjudicates. Do not fix anything.
